newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end quiet session slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end quiet session slightly lower.

text.p: French shares finished fractionally lower after a quiet session as U.S. financial markets were closed for the July 4 holiday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 2.5 points, or 0.09 percent, at 2,934.48. On the week it gained 1.5 percent. The CAC-40 July futures fell two points to 2,938.
Volume was a relatively modest 7.48 billion francs.
Brokers said the dollar's strength helped offset profit-taking on thebourse's recent gains.

Car parts supplier Valeo's stock rose against the grain, climbing 4.25 percent to a record close of 404.50 francs after the company reported a 14.6 percent rise in first-half sales and forecast higher results. Several brokers including BNP Equities and Ferri raised their recommendations on the share.

Shares in defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF rose 2.45 percent to 167 francs, bolstered by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's comments on Thursday evening that the government would be "flexible" and "not ideological" as far as privatisations were concerned.

Lockheed Martin's plan to take over Northrop Grumman turns up pressure on Europeans to form competitive defence giants. Shares in Lagardere, tipped as the favoured bidder for Thomson-CSF, finished up 3.81 percent at 174.50 francs.
